source.name: Proxy: USDA brewed green tea (FDC 171917) for non-caffeine nutrients; caffeine derived from USDA green tea x white/green leaf-caffeine ratio (Hilal & Engelhardt 2007); range from Chin et al. 2008

set.notes: No USDA or CoFID record for white tea. Non-caffeine nutrients are negligible for all plain teas, so brewed green tea values stand in. Caffeine is no longer simply copied from green tea: Hilal & Engelhardt (J Verbr Lebensm 2007; ~30 paired authentic white and green teas from the same areas) measured white-tea leaf caffeine at 4.85 g/100 g (3.35-5.74) against 2.90 g/100 g (1.67-3.90) for the paired green teas, a ratio of ~1.7. Applying that ratio to USDA brewed green tea (12 mg/100 mL) gives ~20 mg/100 mL. This assumes similar extraction; white tea is often brewed cooler, which extracts less, so treat it as an estimate (low confidence). Chin et al. 2008 found 14-61 mg per 6-8 oz serving across white, green and black teas with no trend by tea type, hence the shared range of 6-36 mg/100 mL. The popular claim that white tea is lowest in caffeine is not supported.
